To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) habituation to the presence of the walls can improve navigation in narrow hallways, (2) habituation to stimuli to the sides of a mobile robot does not interfere in its ability to avoid collisions and dead ends.

(a) habituation is a simple, yet effective, learning mechanism that improves the navigation performance in a real mobile robot; (b) habituation to sensory stimulation is not harmful to the robot's ability for obstacle avoidance and turning; (c) the habituation model can be implemented in real robots using only a small number of parameters; (d) the robot's performance can be improved by tuning only a single parameter of the habituation model.
habituation to sensory stimuli can be used to improve the navigation performance of robots in real environments.
